text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm proposing a small schema update and sampling tweak for structured logs that should help correlate GPU capacity flaps with region/network anomalies without increasing storage costs.

alex: I like the idea. High-cardinality fields have been killing our ingest. What are you planning to add exactly?

maria: Two pieces: 1) attach a compact `gpu` label object to infra logs with bounded cardinality (model: `family`, `count_bucket`, `zone_type`) instead of raw instance ids; 2) adjust sampling so we keep 100% of error/latency spikes + 1% of normal traces, and 10% for GPU-related telemetry.

sam: Do we mean keep full JSON for 10% or keep only aggregated metrics? Also what about PII risk in node metadata (hostnames can leak customer IDs)?

maria: Good call. Plan is: for sampled full logs, we redact/freeform-mask any hostnames and `user_email` fields. For the rest we emit a compact event with safe fields only: `ts`, `level`, `region`, `gpu.family`, `gpu.count_bucket`, `reason` (low-cardinality).

jin: Can you show a sample log before/after?

maria: Sure — example of a full-sample GPU utilization alert (before):
```json
{ "ts": "2026-11-10T15:22:01Z", "level": "warn", "node_id": "gpu-az-rt-12345", "hostname": "customer-foo-rt-42-prod", "region": "us-west-2", "gpu": { "model": "A100-80GB", "id": "gpu-0" }, "util": 99.4, "msg": "nvlink errors and throttling observed", "trace": { "alloc": "..." } }
```

maria: After transformation we store (for sampled full payloads):
```json
{ "ts": "2026-11-10T15:22:01Z", "level": "warn", "region": "us-west-2", "gpu.family": "A100", "gpu.count_bucket": "3-4", "msg": "nvlink errors and throttling observed", "node_id_redacted": "node-XXXX", "note": "hostname and trace removed for non-retained events" }
```

leo: How are we defining `count_bucket`? Is that per-pod gpu request or node total?

maria: Node total GPUs available. Buckets: `1`, `2`, `3-4`, `5+`. We want coarse buckets to avoid cardinality explosion.

sam: Where will the redaction live — in the forwarder or ingest service? We should push as early as possible to avoid PII leaving clusters.

maria: Forwarder (fluentd/otel collector) will apply the transform and sampling. Ingest still accepts raw for a short canary window but we won't persist raw past 24h.

qa: What's the canary plan? We should test on one region and GPU pool first.

maria: Canary proposal:
- Week 0: deploy collector transform to `staging` and `canary-us-west-2` (5% of traffic from that region). Keep raw retention 7d there.
- Week 1: monitor SLOs/dashboards (error rate, missing trace correlation, dashboard drift).
- Week 2: increase canary to 25% if no regressions; reduce raw retention to 48h.
- Week 3: global rollout and raw retention 24h with final sampling rates.

alex: Dashboard changes to support this? Grafana panels need to expose the new `gpu.family` and `gpu.count_bucket` fields and update alert queries.

maria: Yes, I'll open a Grafana PR with updated queries and an alert tuning doc. Key alert changes: any spike in `gpu.utilization` combined with `network.error_rate > threshold` for same region within 2m should raise a `gpu-fleet-degraded` alert. We'll tune frequency to avoid noise.

jin: Prometheus label guidance — we should not add `hostname` or `node_id` as labels. Use `region` and `gpu_family` only. Also ensure metrics export uses `zone_type` (edge/core) for routing decisions.

maria: Agreed. Exporter will emit `zone_type` label (`edge`/`core`) and not expose hostnames.

sam: Any perf impact on forwarders from doing JSON masking + sampling? We need numbers.

maria: Early perf tests on a 16-core collector VM: CPU +8-10% at our baseline ingest rate, memory +5%. We'll throttle transforms if CPU > 70% and fall back to lightweight sampling (no redaction) temporarily. That's documented in the deploy playbook.

qa: Can we add a regression test that ensures redaction rules capture obvious patterns (emails, hostnames, IPs)?

maria: Yes — adding unit tests in the collector repo and an integration job that runs on PRs touching transforms.

leo: Will cost change? Lower retention + higher sampling should reduce storage costs. Any estimate?

maria: Estimated -22% in hot storage for logs tied to infra telemetry, with potential -8% overall after rollout. I'll attach a cost model in the PR.

devops-bot: Deployment scheduled: collectors/transform-v2 to canary-us-west-2 at 2026-11-18T02:00:00Z (dry-run).

alex: Thanks. Please add a short rollback procedure in the PR (re-enable raw retention & previous sampler config).

maria: Will do. I'll file the PR and ping this thread. If we get green on the canary by end of week, we can start the 25% step.

sam: 👍 one more ask — include a small dashboard that shows sampling rates over time and fraction of logs redacted so we can monitor signal loss.

maria: Good call, adding that now.

qa: tagging security: @jin please confirm PKI/KMS usage for any node-id hashing we do in upstream pipelines.

jin: Confirmed — we'll use HMAC with KMS-derived key when producing `node_id_redacted` so it is reversible only by infra.

maria: Thanks all — PR link will be here: https://github.com/redwood/collector/pull/XX (will update).

(ends)
